chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has made for the woman the patience of ten men; and when she becomes excited (or passionate), she has the strength of ten men.
ai.seo_question: What does Shia hadith say about the patience and strength of women compared to men?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to elucidate the distinct spiritual and physical constitution of women, asserting that their inherent patience (*sabr*) equals that of ten men. The text further notes that when stirred by emotion or passion, their physical strength multiplies to match that of ten men, a concept often linked to the unique resilience of women in familial and social roles. This teaching underscores the high spiritual status of women in Shia tradition, balancing their emotional intensity with profound endurance.
